_comment: Brokers TradeZulu knows about.
Two jobs. It tells the web interface which brokers to offer and which trade
servers each one has, so nobody has to remember whether their server is
called VantageMarkets-Live or VantageMarkets-Live 8. And it tells the
provisioner which MetaTrader build to install, which the user never sees.
label      what the account form shows
servers    the trade servers to offer. An empty list means the form asks
the user to type one, which is always allowed anyway.
installer  the MetaTrader build to use. Where a broker ships its own, use
it: the generic MetaQuotes terminal cannot resolve a name like
VantageMarkets-Live at all and offers to open a new account
instead, which looks exactly like a rejected password.
matches    substrings that identify this broker from a server name, used
to pick the template. The server name is what decides, because
it always arrives correct -- it comes from the broker.
WHERE THE SERVER LISTS COME FROM, and how to add a broker:
MetaTrader can enumerate them itself, and it is the only authoritative
source -- it asks MetaQuotes. In a terminal: File -> Open an Account, type
the broker's name, press 'Find your company', pick the right legal entity,
Next, then open the Server dropdown. That list is what belongs here.
It cannot be read off disk: the terminal keeps servers.dat encrypted, so
this file is curated from what that dropdown shows rather than generated.
Pick the entity carefully -- 'Vantage' alone returns five companies, and
each has its own servers.

vantage.label: Vantage Markets
vantage._entity: Vantage Markets (Pty) Ltd -- MetaQuotes id VantageMarkets

falcon.label: Falcon Markets
falcon._entity: Falcon Markets Ltd. -- MetaQuotes id FalconMarkets
